There was a 61 MPH measured wind gust at Rockdale. The local newspaper reported downed trees and power lines in and around Rockdale.
Penny size hail was reported 3 miles west of Rockdale.
Several trees were blown down due to high winds in Thorndale. Several power lines were also knocked down after the trees fell on the lines.
Quarter size hail fell about 4 miles northeast of Cameron.
Large tree limbs were blown down and blocked the intersection of Farm-to-Market Road 1600 and County Road 218.
A large tree was blocking Farm-to-Market Road 908 south of Rockdale.
A trained storm spotter reported hail fell 3 miles southwest of Rockdale from 7:15 pm until 7:41 pm. The hail started out pea-sized, but increased to the size of pennies before ending.

Thunderstorm winds peeled the roof off the intake area at the Milano Livestock Exchange. Several trees were also knocked down by the strong winds. Many of the trees were likely already weakened by the extreme drought that had plagued the county over the past year.

Trained spotters reported several trees blown down or destroyed by thunderstorm winds. The tree damage occurred a few miles northeast of the city of Cameron.
Windows were blown out of one side of a house in Ben Arnold.

The Milam County emergency manager reported a mobile home was moved off the foundation piers on Green Street in Rockdale. Several trees were blown down, as were power lines. One Rockdale resident had a large tree fall through her home and she received minor head wounds.

Thunderstorms damaged grain silos and a grain elevator in Thorndale. Several street signs, trees, and structures were also damaged.
A COOP Observer reported a tree that was approximately 40 feet tall fell down on a house in Thorndale.
Emergency management reported roof damage to a few structures in Rockdale, TX.

Am EF-0 tornado occurred in the city of San Gabriel, TX, damaging a business, a church, and a few sheds. Several trees were also damaged in the area. The tornado was on the ground for approximately 0.31 of a mile with a maximum width of 150 yards.
A brief tornado touchdown occurred approximately 5 miles northeast of the city of Cameron, TX. The tornado was rated EF-0 and lasted less than 30 seconds, producing no known damage.
A trained spotter reported two-inch diameter hail approximately 2 miles southeast of the city of Rockdale, TX.
A storm chaser reported two-inch diameter hail approximately 1.3 miles southeast of the city of Rockdale, TX.
A trained spotter reported quarter size hail approximately one mile north-northeast of the city of Milano, TX.
A trained spotter reported golf ball size hail in the city of Rockdale, TX.

Thunderstorm winds damaged a few commercial signs and caused roof damage at a storage facility in the City of Cameron. There was also debris from trees scattered throughout the downtown area.
